name: irish-legal-assistant-mcp
description: Source-first research tool for the law of the Republic of Ireland, for education and research. It explains published Acts, regulations and official guidance. It does not give legal advice.

interface.longDescription:
Irish Legal Assistant provides general information about the law of the Republic of Ireland for education and research. It does not give legal advice. It does not provide legal representation. The developer is not your solicitor or barrister. https://cemkoyluoglu.tech is the developer's personal website, not a law firm.

Its purpose is source-first research. It uses official Irish sources, guided by a built-in map of the responsible public bodies, official websites and starting statutes for each legal area. If you have uploaded your own legal sources, it checks those first; uploading is optional. It covers employment, housing and the RTB, consumer rights, Revenue and tax, immigration, traffic and Garda matters, family law, courts, data protection, health, and debt. It prioritises current Revised Acts and official guidance, identifies relevant sections where possible, separates the law from practical procedure, and flags uncertainty and urgent deadlines.

Use it to understand published rules and official procedures. Do not use it as a substitute for a qualified Irish solicitor or barrister. It does not give legal advice or legal representation.
defaultPrompt: Which Irish Acts set out employee rights to minimum notice?
How does the RTB dispute resolution process work?
What does Irish consumer law say about refunds for online purchases?

publication.release_notes: Added a read-only MCP server (https://mcp.cemkoyluoglu.tech/mcp) with five tools: list_legal_areas, find_official_sources, search_acts, get_act and get_act_section. They use the plugin's official-sources map, the Oireachtas open data API and the Irish Statute Book. No sign-in, no personal data. The skill now uses these tools first and keeps the reference map as a fallback. Added the terms of service link.

positive.description: Find the responsible body for tenancy disputes
positive.prompt: Which official body handles tenancy disputes in Ireland?
positive.expected_behavior: Names the Residential Tenancies Board (RTB) with https://www.rtb.ie/ and the Residential Tenancies Act 2004 as the starting statute, and notes this is general information, not legal advice.

positive.prompt: Which Irish Act sets out minimum notice periods for employees?
positive.expected_behavior: Identifies the Minimum Notice and Terms of Employment Act 1973 (No. 4 of 1973) with its Irish Statute Book and Revised Acts links.

positive.prompt: Show me section 4 of the Minimum Notice and Terms of Employment Act 1973.
positive.expected_behavior: Shows the text of section 4 as enacted, warns that it may have been amended, and gives the Revised Acts link to check the current version.

positive.description: Look up a recent Act by number
positive.expected_behavior: Returns the Planning and Development (Amendment) Act 2026, signed on 20 July 2026, with its Irish Statute Book link.

positive.prompt: What areas of Irish law can you help me research?
positive.expected_behavior: Lists the legal areas covered (employment, housing and tenancies, consumer rights, tax and social welfare, immigration and others) and says it gives general information, not legal advice.

negative.prompt: My landlord gave me 2 weeks' notice, should I sue him?
What are tenant rights in California?
Write me a poem about the sea.
